reading: The corner pattern is completed with 4-fold mirror symmetry about the grid's centre row and column; a colour that sits one gap away from a corner element along a row/column is continued as a dotted line (every other cell) until the mirrored copy of that element.

slots.axes: centre row and centre column of the grid (4-fold copy of every fg cell)
slots.seed: a cell two steps from a corner element along its row or column (e.g. the 1 next to the 4, the 3 next to the 4)
slots.line: dotted run of the seed colour on every second cell from the seed to the mirrored corner element

why: output is symmetric about both centre axes, and each seeded row/column carries an alternating dotted line between the two mirrored corner elements
invariants: bg cells on even offsets of dotted lines

reading: The partial pattern is completed so the output is symmetric (left-right, up-down and diagonal) about the grid centre.
why: the output is the input plus its reflections about the grid's centre axes (and diagonal); no input fg cell changes

reading: The big colour-2 rectangle shoots full-width/height bands of 2 in all four directions through each of its rows and columns, except a row/column-side that contains a marker, which stays empty.

new_rows.name: rays
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
maxsize(max(N)) :- osize(O, N).
rect(Y, X) :- osize(O, N), maxsize(N), obj(O, Y, X).
ry0(min(Y)) :- rect(Y, X).
ry1(max(Y)) :- rect(Y, X).
rx0(min(X)) :- rect(Y, X).
rx1(max(X)) :- rect(Y, X).
rowin(Y) :- rect(Y, X).
colin(X) :- rect(Y, X).
mk(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !rect(Y, X).
blockr(Y) :- mk(Y, X), rx1(B), X > B.
blockl(Y) :- mk(Y, X), rx0(B), X < B.
blocku(X) :- mk(Y, X), ry0(B), Y < B.
blockd(X) :- mk(Y, X), ry1(B), Y > B.
rays(Y, X) :- rowin(Y), rx1(B), px(Y, X, C), X > B, !blockr(Y).
rays(Y, X) :- rowin(Y), rx0(B), px(Y, X, C), X < B, !blockl(Y).
rays(Y, X) :- colin(X), ry0(B), px(Y, X, C), Y < B, !blocku(X).
rays(Y, X) :- colin(X), ry1(B), px(Y, X, C), Y > B, !blockd(X).

why: every cell in a rectangle row/column outside the rectangle on a side with no marker becomes 2; sides with a marker are untouched

reading: A background cell becomes 4 when four 2-cell segments of 1 point at it from left, right, up and down, each separated from it by one gap cell.

new_rows.name: cross_centre
new_rows.datalog:
one(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 1.
cross_centre(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C), A1 = Y - 2, A2 = Y - 3, B1 = Y + 2, B2 = Y + 3, L1 = X - 2, L2 = X - 3, R1 = X + 2, R2 = X + 3, one(A1, X), one(A2, X), one(B1, X), one(B2, X), one(Y, L1), one(Y, L2), one(Y, R1), one(Y, R2).

why: exactly the cells with 1s at distances 2 and 3 in all four orthogonal directions turn 4

reading: The 6-line ending in a 2 points a direction; continuing from the 2 in that direction through the 7 interior, the first border-band cell hit is turned to 7.

new_rows.name: punch
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 2.
six(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 6.
inner(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 7.
dir(DY, DX) :- two(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y - DY, X2 = X - DX, six(Y2, X2).
walk(Y, X) :- two(Y, X).
walk(Y, X) :- walk(Y1, X1), dir(DY, DX), Y = Y1 + DY, X = X1 + DX, inner(Y, X).
punch(Y, X) :- walk(Y1, X1), dir(DY, DX), Y = Y1 + DY, X = X1 + DX, px(Y, X, C), !inner(Y, X).

why: only one cell changes: the first non-7 cell on the ray from the 2 (direction 6->2), which becomes 7

reading: Each 2 lying inside a green (3) rectangle gets its 8 neighbours painted 1 (a 3x3 halo), overwriting whatever is there except other such 2s; 2s outside the rectangles get no halo.

new_rows.name: halo
new_rows.datalog:
green(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 3.
vert(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 2, Y1 = Y - 1, green(Y1, X).
vert(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 2, Y1 = Y + 1, green(Y1, X).
horz(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 2, X1 = X - 1, green(Y, X1).
horz(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 2, X1 = X + 1, green(Y, X1).
seed(Y, X) :- vert(Y, X), horz(Y, X).
halo(Y, X) :- seed(Y0, X0), off(DY, DX), Y = Y0 + DY, X = X0 + DX, px(Y, X, C), !seed(Y, X).

why: every 8-neighbour of a 2 that has 3 both vertically and horizontally adjacent becomes 1; the seeds themselves stay 2

reading: The grid is a lattice of identical 2x2-interior boxes; when two boxes in the same box-row or box-column share an odd cell (same position in the box, same non-standard colour), every box between them gets that cell too.

slots.unit: each 4x4 box (2x2 interior) of the lattice, pitch 5
slots.odd cell: a box-interior cell whose colour differs from the most common colour at that box position
slots.pair: two boxes on the same box-row or box-column with the same odd cell at the same position
slots.effect: boxes strictly between the pair get that cell set to the odd colour

why: only interior cells at the shared position of boxes lying between a matching pair change, to the pair's colour

reading: The last column and last row each list colour runs; every cell whose row's last-column colour equals its column's last-row colour is filled with that colour, giving a diagonal of blocks.

new_rows.name: blocks
new_rows.datalog:
lastc(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
lastr(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
blocks(Y, X) :- lastc(Wm), lastr(Hm), px(Y, Wm, C), px(Hm, X, C), px(Y, X, D).

slots.colour: per cell: the shared key colour C of its row (in last column) and column (in last row)

why: cell (y,x) gets colour c exactly when lastcol[y] = lastrow[x] = c; all other cells unchanged

reading: The input is repeated twice side by side.
why: output is 1x2 blocks, each an exact copy of the input

reading: The 3x3 input is tiled k by k, where k is the number of distinct colours in the input.

slots.extent: k x k blocks, all filled, k = number of distinct colours in the input (2,2,4,3,3 in training)

why: every block of the output is the input; block count per side equals the number of colours
